welcome.title: Ottid listens in Hebrew
welcome.lead: Ottid turns your speech into text — in any app, locally on your machine, with nothing uploaded to the cloud.

microphone.title: So Ottid can hear you
microphone.lead: Ottid needs microphone access to transcribe your speech. Let's check it works.

hardware.title: Ottid tunes itself to your machine
hardware.lead: Ottid checks how powerful your machine is and picks models that will run well on it. You can change the choice any time.

tongue.title: The small creature living on your screen
tongue.lead: This is Ottid, a dark puddle with two hands and ember eyes. The lamp inside shows what it is doing, and it is always lit while Ottid listens. Drag it to the taskbar or the top edge, or leave it floating.

hotkey.title: One key opens dictation
hotkey.lead: A single press of Ctrl+Space opens listening. Speak Hebrew — and when you finish, the text appears wherever the cursor is.

practice.title: Try it now
practice.lead: Press Ctrl+Space and say a short sentence in Hebrew — I'll show you here exactly what Ottid heard.

done.title: That's it — you know how to use Ottid
done.lead: You can always reopen this tutorial from the tray menu, next to the clock.

warmup.label: Ottid is getting ready for first use
warmup.hint: A one-time download — the next launch is instant.

mic.ready: Excellent — Ottid can hear your microphone.
mic.noDevice: No microphone found. Connect one and check again.
mic.blocked: Ottid couldn't open the microphone. Grant microphone access in your system settings, then check again.
mic.hint: Recording stays on your machine — no audio is sent anywhere.

states.dictateBlurb: What you say is typed wherever the cursor is.
states.commandBlurb: A single sentence that gets done — "open Slack", "mute everything".
states.chatBlurb: Free-form voice conversation. Memory stays with you.

howto.step2: Speak Hebrew in a normal voice.
howto.step3: Stop speaking, or press again — and the text is dictated.
howto.fineprint: These are the three chords. We'll only practise the first one for now.

practice.or: Or anything else you like — Ottid listens to it all.
practice.hint: You don't have to practise to continue — but it's much more fun to see it work.
practice.heardHint: This is what Ottid heard. In real use it would be typed wherever your cursor is.

discord.title: Discord mute during dictation (experimental)
discord.intro: Temporarily hold Discord Push to Mute during recording and transcription. Manual mute stays unchanged. Windows desktop Discord, Voice Activity mode.
discord.step1: In Discord: User Settings → Keybinds → Add a Keybind → Push to Mute. Reserve F24 for this action only.
discord.step2: Click Send F24 here, then switch to the Discord keybind recorder within five seconds. Finish recording the shortcut and leave the Keybinds page.
discord.step3: Test for six seconds. Check that Discord stops transmitting and resumes on its own. Repeat while manually muted: it must stay muted.
discord.settingUp: Switch to Discord and record the shortcut now…
discord.testing: F24 is held for six seconds. Check Discord transmission…
discord.checkResult: Request sent. Check the result in Discord; Ottid cannot verify its mute state.
discord.failed: The key guard could not run. Automatic suppression remains unverified.
discord.verified: I verified both automatic release and preservation of manual mute
discord.enable: Mute me in Discord while dictating
discord.enableHint: Ottid temporarily mutes you from the start of recording until transcription finishes, then releases the temporary mute. If you were manually muted, you stay muted.
discord.limit: No mute acknowledgement is available. Recheck after changing Discord keybinds, input mode or permissions. Other apps remain outside this integration.
discord.windowsOnly: Available for Discord desktop on Windows.
discord.captureBlocked: Discord suppression unavailable — recording did not start.

general.title: General
general.languageHint: Choose the language Ottid's interface is shown in. The change applies to every window immediately.
general.placementHint: Where Ottid stands: on the taskbar, floating on the desktop, or hanging from the top of the screen. You can also drag it to an edge.

hardware.title: Hardware
hardware.intro: The hardware tier sets how Ottid runs speech recognition — probing the GPU, or staying on the CPU. Ottid never changes it silently; the choice is yours.
hardware.sttDeviceGpu: On this tier, speech recognition uses the GPU when one is available.
hardware.sttDeviceCpu: On this tier, speech recognition runs on the CPU.
hardware.restartToApply: Restart Ottid for this change to take effect.

wakeword.title: Wake words
wakeword.intro: Ottid listens for two independent wake words — one starts hands-free dictation, the other runs a Command-mode tool chain. Pick a different classifier for each slot.
wakeword.enableHint: When on, Ottid listens in the background for this wake word.
wakeword.modelHint: Pick which classifier this slot listens for. The other slot's model is hidden so each word maps to one mode.

dictation.title: Dictation slot
dictation.hint: When this wake word fires, the next thing you say is typed into the focused field — like the dictation hotkey.

llm.title: Language models
llm.intro: Ottid can call a language model for two different modes — Command mode (M8) and Chat mode (M8). The cloud is always opt-in and badged, and your API keys never touch settings.json.
llm.commandHint: The model that turns voice commands into PC actions.
llm.chatHint: The model that answers free-form questions in conversation.

about.title: About
about.tagline: A local-first voice assistant that listens in Hebrew.
about.localFirst: All processing happens on your machine. No recording or text is sent to the cloud.

voice.title: Voice corrections
voice.intro: Token-level substitutions applied to the STT transcript before either the recipe cascade or the LLM planner sees it. Useful for proper nouns Whisper keeps mishearing ("cloud" instead of "claude"), contact-name homonyms, and any word that consistently lands wrong.

agents.title: Coding agents
agents.intro: When Claude Code needs permission to run a command or edit a file, Ottid can show the request on its approval card, where you allow or deny it without going back to the terminal. If Ottid is closed, or nobody answers in time, Claude Code asks in the terminal as usual.

state.on: Connected in the settings file below. Claude Code sessions using this file can show permission requests on Ottid's card.
state.off: Not connected. Claude Code asks in the terminal.
state.stale: Connected to another copy of Ottid. Connecting again points it at this one.
state.missing: This build has no hook client (ottid-hook), so it can't connect.
state.unreadable: Ottid can't read Claude Code's settings file, so it won't change it.

agents.missingHint: In a local build, build it with:
agents.notListening: The hook is installed, but Ottid couldn't open its listener, so requests go back to the terminal. Restarting Ottid should fix it.
agents.hooksDisabled: disableAllHooks is on in the settings file, so Claude Code runs no hooks, Ottid's included.
agents.requirements: Requires Claude Code 2.1.139 or newer. Ottid reads CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR from its own environment. If Claude Code uses a different folder, the installed hook will not run there; connected means the entry exists in the file shown above.
agents.codexRequirements: Use a Codex build with PermissionRequest hooks (validated with CLI 0.142.5). After connecting, open /hooks in Codex and review and trust the new hook. Restart or start a new local session. Ottid cannot detect hook trust or managed restrictions.
agents.codexScope: Installed in user hooks.json under CODEX_HOME from Ottid's environment, or ~/.codex. Connected means the entry exists in the displayed file. Project, plugin and managed hooks may also run. No approval policy is changed.
agents.codexDisabled: Codex hooks can be disabled with features.hooks=false or restricted by managed policy. Enable and review them in Codex; Ottid does not change those settings.
agents.scope: The hook goes into Claude Code's user settings (user scope), so it applies to every project. Hooks set in a project or in local settings keep running alongside it.
agents.once: An answer on the card covers that one request; Ottid never adds standing permissions.
agents.privacy: Requests stay on this computer, on a channel only your user account can open. Ottid neither keeps what a request contains nor writes it to its log.

error.no-home: The user's home folder wasn't found.
error.no-hook-binary: This build has no hook client (ottid-hook).

error.not-json: The settings file isn't valid JSON. Fix it by hand first.
error.not-object: The settings file isn't a JSON object.

error.changed: The file changed since the preview. This is the change against the file as it is now; look it over again.
